design_summary.purpose: Synthesizable FPGA top module for adaptive aero control that exposes a compact register window and one bounded request/response streaming path to an external GPU/NIM worker running the pretrained DoMINO automotive-aero model in software. The RTL is limited to transport, configuration, validation, safety, timeout handling, bounded command generation, and deterministic fallback behavior.
design_summary.operating_model: Software configures session metadata, request thresholds, command bounds, and fault-clear controls through the register block. The top-level composes a fixed-width outbound request, presents it over valid/ready handshaking, accepts only matching responses, rejects stale or invalid responses, maps accepted model output into a 32-bit actuator command, clamps the command to configured limits, and asserts fallback behavior whenever enable, validation, timeout, or freshness conditions require it. Geometry is treated as an external descriptor/token rather than on-chip geometry storage.

module_architecture.name: adaptive_aero_control_regfile
responsibilities: Decode register writes and produce stable configuration outputs.

Expose enable, soft reset, pipelined mode, sequence seed, timeout threshold, response age limit, actuator limits, fallback command, stream velocity, flow-condition metadata, geometry format, geometry source, and geometry token fields.
Provide software-readable status and latest accepted command snapshot via register read path.
Generate explicit status-clear and issue-request control strobes.
Treat geometry as external metadata/token rather than an on-chip geometry array.
Support supplied reference metadata values for stream_velocity_mps=38.89, geometry_format=STL, and geometry_source=DrivAerML reference geometry.
interface_notes: Consumes the compact 8-bit register address, 32-bit write data, and read/write strobes.
Drives configuration and control outputs used by request packaging, validation, command mapping, and safety gating.
Consumes top-level status and latest command snapshots for software observability.
Does not drive any clock, reset, or input-side register signals.
ownership_notes: Owns cfg_enable, cfg_soft_reset, cfg_pipelined_mode, cfg_seq_seed, cfg_request_timeout, cfg_response_age_limit, cfg_max_act_cmd, cfg_min_act_cmd, cfg_fallback_cmd, cfg_stream_velocity_mps, cfg_flow_condition, cfg_geometry_format, cfg_geometry_source, cfg_geom_token, cfg_status_clear, cfg_issue_request, and reg_rdata.
The geometry-related outputs are control-plane descriptors only and not geometry storage.

module_architecture.name: adaptive_aero_request_packager
module_architecture.role: Outbound request composer for the external GPU/NIM worker
responsibilities: Compose the 128-bit outbound request packet.
Include transaction ID, sequence counter, configuration snapshot, flow-condition values, geometry metadata, and geometry token fields.
Assert req_valid only when a request is ready and the external bridge is available.
Hold req_data stable until req_ready is observed.
Do not launch a second request while one is outstanding in default single-outstanding mode.
Support pipelined mode only when explicitly enabled by configuration.
interface_notes: Consumes enable and pipelined-mode control from the register block along with sequence seed and configuration metadata.
Consumes request issuance control and inflight state from the top-level control path.
Drives req_data, req_valid, and request_issued to the top-level transport path.
Uses req_ready as the downstream handshake qualifier and holds the payload stable until acceptance.
ownership_notes: The payload is fixed-width and software-defined; it carries metadata/control descriptors only, not raw geometry or tensor content.

module_architecture.name: adaptive_aero_response_validator
module_architecture.role: Inbound response checking and acceptance stage
responsibilities: Compare response transaction ID and sequence with the outstanding request.
Reject responses that arrive after timeout or beyond the response age limit.
Gate acceptance on model-present and model-enabled status bits.
Preserve safe fallback behavior when validation fails.
Emit explicit validation-failed, stale-rejected, and timeout-hit indicators.
Provide accepted model response data only when the response passes all checks.
interface_notes: Consumes 128-bit rsp_data and rsp_valid from the external worker stream.
Uses expected transaction and sequence identifiers, watchdog count, timeout threshold, response age limit, enable, and model-present indicators from the top-level control path.
Drives rsp_ready, accepted, validation_failed, stale_rejected, timeout_hit, and accepted_model_data into downstream command mapping and safety gating.
Does not alter actuator outputs directly; it only qualifies response acceptance.
ownership_notes: Owns rsp_ready, accepted, validation_failed, stale_rejected, timeout_hit, and accepted_model_data.
Accepted model data is a forwarding path for model output fields, not a physics computation.

module_architecture.name: adaptive_aero_command_mapper
responsibilities: Convert accepted model output fields into a 32-bit command word.
Remain abstract and configuration-driven.
Avoid any physics surrogate or geometry inference in RTL.
Provide a valid mapped command only when input response acceptance is asserted.
interface_notes: Consumes the accepted flag and accepted model data from the validator.
Consumes command bounds and fallback configuration from the register block.
Produces mapped_cmd and mapped_cmd_valid for the safety gate.
Does not assume a specific actuator topology or mechanical package.
ownership_notes: The command encoding is defined by software/integration registers rather than hardwired mechanical assumptions.

module_architecture.name: adaptive_aero_safety_gate
module_architecture.role: Final safety, saturation, fallback, and telemetry aggregation stage
responsibilities: Clamp mapped commands to configured min/max bounds.
Assert saturation when limiting occurs.
Drive fallback command when validation fails, timeout expires, enable is deasserted, or stale response is detected.
Hold fallback-active until a fresh valid response is accepted.
Generate status telemetry with busy, ready-for-request, response-pending, response-accepted, validation-failed, stale-rejected, timeout, saturation, fallback-active, and enable bits.
Deassert act_cmd_valid when the module is disabled or no valid command is available.
interface_notes: Consumes validation outcomes, mapped command data, enable and soft-reset control, status-clear and request-issue control, and command bounds/fallback configuration.
Consumes lifecycle indicators busy, ready_for_request, response_pending, and response_accepted from the top-level control path.
Drives the final act_cmd_out, act_cmd_valid_out, saturation, fallback_active, and status_word outputs.
Acts as the final authority on actuator output validity.
ownership_notes: Owns saturation, fallback_active, status_word, act_cmd_out, and act_cmd_valid_out.
Clamping and fallback are deterministic and fixed-width, with no floating-point dependency.

interface_summary.intent: Provide the compact software-visible register window for configuration, status readback, and command snapshot access.
Compose and launch a bounded outbound request packet while preserving stable payload behavior until downstream acceptance.
Accept only matching, non-stale responses and produce qualified model data and response health indicators.
Translate accepted model output fields into a deterministic 32-bit actuator command word under configuration control.
Apply saturation, timeout/fallback policy, and final status aggregation before exposing the actuator command and status outputs.

data_flow_summary: Software programs the register file with enable, soft reset, request timeout, response age limit, command bounds, fallback command, sequence seed, flow-condition metadata, and geometry descriptor/token values.

The request packager composes a fixed-width 128-bit request using the transaction ID, sequence counter, configuration snapshot, flow-condition values, and geometry descriptor/token, then asserts req_valid only when the request can be safely launched.

The external worker returns rsp_data on the streaming response path; the response validator checks transaction identity, sequence, enable/model-present gating, watchdog timeout, and response-age limit before accepting the response.
Accepted response data is forwarded to the command mapper, which converts the model output into a deterministic 32-bit command word according to software-defined encoding rules.

The safety gate clamps the mapped command to configured bounds, substitutes fallback command on invalid or stale conditions, asserts saturation when clipping occurs, and publishes the final status word and actuator outputs.
During reset or fault conditions, the top-level remains in safe fallback state with act_cmd_valid deasserted until a fresh valid response is accepted and the enable path permits actuation.

clock_reset_summary.clocking: Single synchronous clk domain is assumed for control, register, request, response, and safety-state logic. Valid/ready streaming handshakes are used for the external request and response paths. Control state is implemented with flip-flops only; geometry and payload content are not stored as bulk RTL arrays.
clock_reset_summary.reset_behavior: On rst_n deassertion, the module enters safe fallback state, clears outstanding transaction state, clears timeout, stale, validation-failed, and saturation flags, deasserts act_cmd_valid and req_valid, and asserts fallback-active status. The register block clears control strobes and initializes configuration outputs to safe defaults. The design keeps the command path disabled until enable is configured and a valid command is available; fallback-active remains indicated after reset until the first accepted response produces a valid command.

integration_notes: The design intentionally omits physics surrogate computation, tensor processing, geometry meshing, and flow-field inference in RTL; those functions are external to the FPGA IP.
Geometry is carried only as a metadata field or memory token; no on-chip geometry model, geometry array, or large payload store is implied.

A shallow, control-oriented memory wrapper may be used only if needed for bounded request/response bookkeeping; it should map to native block RAM in FPGA flow and must not be flattened into registers.
The default operating mode is single-outstanding-transaction; pipelined operation is only permitted when explicitly configured.

The outbound request and inbound response payload formats are fixed-width and integration-defined by software; RTL should treat payload fields as transport descriptors rather than semantic geometry or physics content.

Status telemetry must remain readable by software for monitoring, fault clearing, and session management, including busy, ready-for-request, response-pending, response-accepted, validation-failed, stale-rejected, timeout, saturation, fallback-active, and enable bits.
The implementation must avoid Sky130 hard macro usage and target FPGA-friendly synthesis conventions only.
Top-level scalar-equivalent I/O remains within the required bound and is limited to the specified ports.
consistency_notes: No hierarchy, ports, or filenames may differ from digital_spec_json.
